info.title: arr-metadata-server
info.description:
A self-hosted metadata server for the *arr stack.

It answers three client protocols from one store — Sonarr's Skyhook API, Radarr's metadata API, and the TMDB v3 API — alongside its own API, documented here in full, and it is a metadata provider Plex Media Server can be given, under `/plex`. TheTVDB's v4 API and AniList's are relayed to the real services, with the fields locked here written into their answers.

**Locks.** Any field a person edits is recorded separately from provider data and is never overwritten by a refresh. That is what the `/items/{id}/overrides` routes manage, and what `lockedFields` reports.

**Authentication differs per surface.** Sonarr and Radarr have their metadata URLs compiled in and cannot attach a credential, and Plex sends none to a provider, so those routes are guarded by address rather than by key. The routes documented without a security requirement are those; they are not open.

get.summary:
Relay any TMDB v3 request, with this server's locks written in on the way
back.
get.description:
The request goes upstream with this server's own credentials substituted
for whatever the client sent — or, when `tmdb.relayCredential` is
`client`, with the client's own TMDB key or token as it came, a key issued
here being refused with a 401 that says why. If the path addresses a
title a person locked fields on, those fields are written into the
upstream document before it is returned, so the client gets TMDB's full
response with the operator's corrections in it. A text — a title, an
overview — is written as it is locked for the language the client asked
(`language=`, TMDB's `en-US` when none is): locked in that language, or in
every one. One locked in another language alone leaves TMDB's own text in
the one asked.

Every TMDB v3 path is accepted; see TMDB's own documentation for their
shapes. Patched: `/3/movie/{id}`, `/3/tv/{id}`, `/3/tv/{id}/season/{n}`,
`/3/tv/{id}/season/{n}/episode/{e}`, and the results of
`/3/search/{movie,tv,multi}`, `/3/trending/{movie,tv,all}/{window}` and
`/3/discover/{movie,tv}`.

get.summary:
What airs and what comes out in a window: the episodes of every series,
and the films out in cinemas, digitally or on disc.
get.description:
An episode by the moment it airs, in UTC — where no provider knew the
time, midnight UTC on its date, which is what Sonarr is given; a release
by its day, at midnight UTC too, once for each day a film comes out. A
film's days are the reader's country's where its releases there are
known, its own otherwise, and a day somebody corrected by hand stays as
they put it. The window is the caller's to choose, so a day is the
caller's own day wherever it is. Switched off, or for adults where the
reader would not be shown one, a work is left out of both.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: The first instant of the window, RFC 3339: `2026-09-21T22:00:00Z`.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: The instant the window ends, not included. At most 62 days after `from`.

parameters.description: Titles in this language, where a translation is held.

parameters.description:

the days it comes out there, where those are known, and on its own
dates otherwise. Absent, the country this caller is answered for:
`tmdb.watchRegion` as set for it, else its language's.

400.description: The window is not two instants, or is longer than 62 days, or the region is not a country code

salles`. Subscribe a calendar app to it — as `webcal://` — and the week's
episodes and films are in it, refreshed as the app sees fit.

get.summary:

get.description:
A bearer token that is a key issued here is this server's business: the
operator's own TheTVDB token takes its place, and the client's copy never
leaves. Any other token is the client's own, and travels as it came. A
caller with no token who authenticated with a key — in the header or the
query — is asked for with the operator's token too. The operator's own
account, `user` and what hangs off it, is nobody else's: refused with
the operator's token, read with a client's own. With each client's own
key relayed (`tvdb.relayCredential = client`), the operator's token is
never used, and a key issued here is refused with a 401 that says why.

Every v4 path is accepted; see TheTVDB's own documentation for their
shapes. The documents about a work of this catalogue are the ones patched:
`series/{id}` and `movies/{id}`, both `/extended` — with the translations,
seasons and episodes asked with them — and `/translations/{lang}`; a page
of a series' episodes in any of its orders, `[/{lang}]`; `seasons/{id}`
and its `/extended`; one episode, `/extended` and `/translations/{lang}`.

[`Surface`]: Sonarr and Radarr share a guard, but not a switch.

keyPrefix.description: The visible head of the key, e.g. `ams_a1b2c3d4`.

ownerId.description: The account it belongs to; none for a server key.

enabled.description: Whether an administrator left it on.

policy.description:
What it asks of a caller. Set by the deployment's environment, not
here — except that a relay asked with each client's own key asks for
a listed address where the environment says a key.

served.description: Calls answered and refused since the server started.

pushRefresh.description: Whether a change here is told to them.

waiting.description: Works changed here and not told yet, on the instance answering.

pushes.description: The latest works told of, newest first.

ArrConnection.description: One of the two, as set.

keySet.description: Whether a key is kept. It is never sent back.

ready.description: An address and a key both set: this server reaches it.

ArrPush.description: One work told of, as the page lists it.

clientId.description: The id the work is served under.

arrId.description: Its own id there, when it holds the work.

detail.description: The command it went in, or what went wrong.

ArrStatus.description: What a status says of the one that answered.

instanceName.description: The name it was given, when it was given one.

url.description: The address to try; the stored one when left out.

key.description:
The key to try with; the stored one when left out — which is tried
only at the origin it was kept for, the stored address's scheme, host
and port.

oneOf.description: Who answered, and in which version.

error.description: What went wrong, in words that name neither the address nor the key.

sonarrUrl.description:
Left out, the address stays; empty, it is removed — and the key kept
with it.

sonarrKey.description:
Left out, the stored key stays; empty, it is removed. Given again
whenever the address moves to another scheme, host or port: a key
kept goes to no other.

origin.description: The address it was fetched from, or `upload:<id>` for an upload.

key.description: Where the bytes are, once stored: `<sha256>.<ext>`.

color.description: The colour most of a picture is, `#rrggbb`, once worked out.

thumbhash.description: A picture's ThumbHash, base64, once worked out.

wantedBy.description: The work that wanted it first.

AssetCounts.description: The tallies the media page opens on.

bytes.description: Of what is stored, in bytes.

AttachCredits.description: The credits filed under a person.

credits.description:
The credits, by id — a work's `credits[].id` — whomever they were
filed under.

target.description: What was acted on: an item id, a client name, a field path.

detail.description: A short human-readable note. Never carries a secret.

oneOf.description:
The work the target names, when it names one still held: its title,
for a reader who does not know works by their ids.

actions.description: Every action name, so a UI can offer them as filters without hard-coding.

nextCursor.description:
Where the next page begins: give it back as `cursor`. Absent after
the last page.

site.description:
`public`: anyone browses the catalogue. `private`: every page asks to
sign in first.

passwordLogin.description: Whether the password form is offered to everyone.

oneOf.description: The identity provider's button, when signing in through one is on.

webp.description:
Whether the pages are given WebP copies of the pictures this server
keeps (`media.webp`), rather than the pictures themselves: said here,
where every page reads it before it draws one.

Backup.description: An archive, as the Backups page lists it.

sizeBytes.description: Its size where it is kept, in bytes.

engine.description:
The engine its database was read from — `sqlite` or `postgres` —
when this database describes it.

serverVersion.description: The version of the server that made it, the same way.

migration.description: The last migration its database had, the same way.

createdBy.description:
Who asked for it, as the journal names them; `null` for the schedule
and for one this database does not describe.

sha256.description:
The SHA-256 of the archive as kept, when this database describes it:
what a copy taken elsewhere is checked against.

present.description:
Whether it is where the archives are kept. One removed by hand is
still listed while this database describes it, and can only be
forgotten.

described.description:
Whether this database describes it. One put where the archives are
kept by hand — or made before a restore brought back an older list —
is listed from its name alone; its manifest says the rest.

upgradeTo.description:
For an archive made before an upgrade, the migration the start went
on to apply: the database in it is at `migration`, the one before.

BackupList.description: The archives, where they are kept, and how the server makes them.

place.description:
`directory`, or `bucket` among several instances whose media are in
one.

location.description: Where: the directory's path, or the bucket and its folder.

encrypted.description:
Whether the archives the server makes are encrypted:
`AMS_BACKUP_PASSPHRASE` is set.

mediaOnDisk.description: Whether an archive can carry the media: they are kept on disk.

mediaStore.description: Where the media are kept: `off`, `filesystem` or `s3`.

keep.description: How many of the schedule's archives are kept.

includeMedia.description: Whether the schedule's archives carry the media kept on disk.

lastAt.description: When the newest archive was made.

nextAt.description: When the schedule makes the next; `null` while it is off.

overdue.description:
Whether the newest archive is older than twice the schedule's
interval, or there is none, while the schedule is on.

oneOf.description: The run making one now, when one is.

format.description: The archive's layout: [`FORMAT`] when this server wrote it.

server.description: The version of the server that made it.

migration.description: The last migration its database had.

engine.description:
The engine the database was read from: `sqlite` or `postgres`.
Restored onto either.

reason.description:
Why it was made: `scheduled`, `manual`, `safety`, `command`, or
`upgrade` — by a start, before the migrations it went on to apply.

upgradeTo.description:
For an archive made before an upgrade, the last migration the start
went on to apply.

files.description: Each file but the media, with its size and SHA-256.

BackupMedia.description: What the archive holds of the media.

included.description: Whether the media kept on disk are in it, under `media/`.

store.description:
Where the server it was made of kept them: `off`, `filesystem` or
`s3`.

note.description:
What a restore has to know: where the media are when they are not
here.

BackupMediaCheck.description: The media the database names, against the media the store holds.

missing.description:
Named by a row, not in the store: served from its provider's
address until it is fetched again.

unreferenced.description: In the store, named by no row: the sweep takes these away.

BackupReason.description: Why an archive was made: said in its name, and in its row.

BackupRequest.description: What an archive made now is to hold.

includeMedia.description:
The media kept on disk with the database. Left out, as the
schedule's archives have them.

BackupRestore.description: Where the last restore this instance ran stands.

error.description: What went wrong; the database is as it was before.

oneOf.description: What was restored, once it was.

BackupRestoreRequest.description: What opens the archive to restore.

passphrase.description:
Its passphrase, when it is encrypted with another than the server's
own. Never kept, never logged.

archive.description: The archive restored, by its name or its path.

safety.description:
The archive made of the database before it was replaced: what
undoes this restore. `null` when the database was empty.

rows.description: The rows copied into the database.

mediaRestored.description: The media the archive held that were put back into the store.

mediaSkipped.description:
Those it held that were not: the store already had them, or there
is no store to put them in.

oneOf.description:
How the media the restored rows name stand in the store, when there
is one.

Base.description: One of the ways into MyAnimeList.

failedAt.description: When it last failed to answer, while it is passed over for it.

BatchPreviewRequest.description: Lines to set beside the catalogue.

lines.description:
A work a line: an id, or its page at a provider. Two thousand at the
most.

oneOf.description:
What a TMDB id stands for where its line does not say: `movie` or
`series`.

lines.description: A work a line, as the preview reads them. Two thousand at the most.

oneOf.description: What a TMDB id stands for where its line does not say.

language.description:
A language the episode texts of each series imported are fetched in
at once, besides the catalogue's own: `fr`, `pt-BR`.

lists.description:
The hand-made selections the works go into, held already or
imported, by id or slug. Twenty at the most.

enabled.description:
Whether the works imported are switched on; those held already keep
what they are. On when absent.

jobId.description: The run, as the tasks page follows it.

works.description: How many works it takes, each once.

passedOver.description: How many lines named none: not an id, or a TMDB id of no kind.

value.description: The role or status, for those two.

CacheSpace.description: One of the caches, by the name it is filed under.

entries.description:
The episodes and the films' releases together, earliest first: an
episode at its moment, a release at midnight UTC on its day, and of
two at the same moment the episode first.

works.description:
Every work the entries belong to, drawn as a list is: artwork and
scores, no episodes.

truncated.description:
The window held more episodes, or more releases, than one answer
carries, and the latest are missing: ask for a shorter one.

allOf.description:
An episode, and the work it belongs to. Boxed: an episode is four
times a release, and a window holds hundreds of either.

oneOf.description:
An episode, and the work it belongs to. Boxed: an episode is four
times a release, and a window holds hundreds of either.

allOf.description: A film's release: in cinemas, digitally, on disc.

oneOf.description: A film's release: in cinemas, digitally, on disc.

CalendarEntry.description: One thing the schedule lists: an episode airing, or a film coming out.

hostname.description: What the resolver and the hosts file call this address, if anything.

userAgent.description: What the caller called itself. Sonarr and Radarr say so plainly.

covered.description:
Whether a rule covers this address *now*, which is not the same question
as `last_allowed` — that one is about the call this row last recorded,
and a rule added since has not changed it. Filled in by the handler,
which is the only place that holds the live allowlist.

Candidate.description: A work premiering in the season that this server does not hold.

CreditId.description: Radarr stores this with a NOT NULL constraint.

countries.description:
The countries the works were made in, ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, most common
first — counted as if no country were chosen.

certifications.description:
The ratings the works carry in the reader's country (`region`), as
that country writes them; mildest first where they are ages, most
common first otherwise. Counted as if no rating were chosen.

region.description:
The country those ratings are read in: the one asked for, else the
one this caller is answered for. Absent, the ratings are the ones the
works carry as their own.

CatalogueFacets.description:
What the catalogue can be narrowed by next, with how many works each
choice would leave: the list's facets, and the countries and the ratings
its further filters choose among.

fingerprint.description: SHA-256, as a browser shows it.

ChangeEntry.description: A change, as the journal reads it.

actor.description:
Who, as the audit trail names them — a person, or a key; nothing for
the schedule's own doing.

provider.description: The source whose answer the new value is, where one is known.

scope.description:
`item`, `season:2`, `episode:2x5`, or a child a lock names, as a lock
names it: `credit:actor:tmdb:17419`.

field.description:
The field, as the field registry names it; for an episode, `number`
when it moved, `episode` when it came or went — `season` for a season.

language.description:
The language a text was locked in alone (`fra`); absent for every
language, and for what is in none.

wasLocked.description:
Whether a lock held the field as it changed: a source's change made
under one reached the record and not what is served.

ChangeList.description: A page of a work's journal.

changes.description:
Newest first; the changes one write made, in the order the work
lists them.

next.description:
What to ask for the next page with, as `cursor`; absent after the
last.

fields.description: Every field the work's journal names, for a filter to offer.

who.description: Everybody it names — people, keys, sources — for a filter to offer.

from.description: The quarter's first and last days.

works.description:
Every work the entries belong to, drawn as a list draws them: artwork,
scores and titles in the reader's language, no episodes.

name.description: TMDB's name for it, where a key lets it be asked.

count.description: How many of its films the catalogue holds.

items.description: The films the catalogue holds, in release order, drawn as a list is.

parts.description: Every film of the collection as TMDB lists it, marked where it is held.

held.description: The catalogue's own id, where the film is in it.

Parts.description:
A movie may belong to a collection, and a collection holds movies. That
loop makes schema collection recurse forever unless it is cut here.

Compared.description: One work of the two, as the comparison draws it.

work.description:
The work as a card draws it — its pictures, its scores, its running
time, its genres — without its seasons, episodes or credits.

seasons.description: A series' seasons, its specials aside.

episodes.description: A series' episodes, its specials aside.

shared.description:
The people both credit, as the works' own credits file them — their
casts and crews, not single episodes' — those who made them first,
then by their billing.

CountryRelease.description:
What a work was given in one country: a day it came out there and how,
the rating it carries there, or both.

oneOf.description:
How it came out there; none for a rating given without a release —
a series' ratings, and Radarr's.

note.description: What TMDB notes beside it: a festival, a service, a re-release.

CoverType.description:
Cover types, using Sonarr and Radarr's spelling so the compatibility
surfaces can emit them without a translation table.

key.description: Shown once. It is not recoverable afterwards — only its hash is stored.

maxUses.description: How many accounts it may open; one when left out.

days.description: Days it lasts; seven when left out, and never more than a year.

note.description: Who it is for, for the administrators' memory. Never shown to them.

password.description:
Twelve characters at least. Left out, one is generated and returned —
once.
The generated password, when none was given. Shown once.

creditTmdbId.description:
TMDB's identifier for *this role*, distinct from the person's id. Radarr
requires it and rejects a credit without one.

CreditEdit.description: What may be changed of a credit. Each key left out stands as it is.

hidden.description:
`true` keeps a credit a source gave out of every answer; `false`
gives it back. A credit added by hand is removed instead.

characterName.description:
The character played: a string corrects it — an empty one says there
is none — and `null` lifts the correction.

sortOrder.description:
Its place among the credits of its kind, lower first: a number moves
it, `null` lifts the correction.

CreditId.description: Radarr stores this with a NOT NULL constraint.

slug.description: What the list is addressed by, derived from its name.

oneOf.description: The filter, for a list composed by one.

isPublic.description:
Whether a reader with no credential may see it, where public browsing
is on at all.

cover.description:
The picture the selection is shown with, by the address it goes by —
a provider's, or an upload's `upload:` origin. The store holds it so;
what a reader is given is the copy kept, where there is one, which is
the API's to put in its place.

itemCount.description:
How many works a hand-made list holds, of those switched on; a
filter's are counted as they are read, and this is nought.

items.description:
The works, drawn as a list is: artwork and scores, no episodes. For a
reader, those the reader may see; for whoever maintains the list,
every member, so one that is switched off or of the other kind can
be taken out.

CuratedListRequest.description:
What a list is made of. Every field is optional: on creation the absent
ones take their defaults, on a change they are left as they are — a
change that says nothing about visibility does not publish a draft.

cover.description:
The picture the selection is shown with, by its address — a
provider's, which the catalogue holds a copy of or not, or any
`https://` address: the site's pages load no picture over `http://`.
Empty, it is taken away; left out, it stays.

items.description:
The members of a hand-made list, in order; left as they are when
absent.

Dataset.description: A list downloaded whole, as the Sources page says of it.

task.description: The task that downloads it, on the Jobs page.

on.description: Whether a switch that needs it is on.

everySeconds.description: Seconds between two downloads, by its own cadence.

oneOf.description:
When it last landed, and how many of its rows were kept; absent
until it has landed once.
How its last run ended, whether it landed or not.

lastRunAt.description: When its last run ended, or began while it runs.

nextAt.description: When the schedule downloads it next, while it is on.

scopes.description: Where this may be set. Anything narrower than the first entry overrides.

Discovery.description: What discovery found, for the administrator checking the configuration.

keys.description: Keys in the provider's key set.

first.description: One work of the pair, by its id.

mode.description:
`authority`: a certificate this server issues itself; `own`: the
operator's files.

refused.description:
Names asked for that the authority may not certify: its constraints
were set when it was made.

renewBeforeDays.description: A certificate with fewer days left than this is renewed.

DoorMode.description: Whose certificate the clients' door shows.

DuplicateConfidence.description: How sure the server is that two works are one.

pairs.description:
Surest first: an identifier shared, then a title, then an IMDb id on
a film and a series.

DuplicateReason.description: Why two works look like one.

DuplicateView.description: A pair of duplicates as the catalogue shows it.

detail.description:
What they share: an identifier as `imdb:tt0903747`, or the title as
it was folded.

survivor.description: The one of the two the rule would keep.

key.description:
Which one it is about: a work's or a selection's id, a genre's or a
network's slug, a year, the first year of a decade.

language.description: The language it is written in: `en`, `fr`.

body.description: What it says, in the restricted Markdown.

updatedBy.description: Who wrote it last, as the journal names people: `editor:alice`.

body.description:
What it says: paragraphs, `*emphasis*`, `**strong emphasis**` and
`[links](/genre/drama)` to pages of this site, at most three thousand
characters. Empty, the note in this language is taken away.

Effective.description:
One setting as the interface shows it: what it is, and where the answer
currently comes from.

source.description:
The scope the value was found at — `server` unless something narrower
overrode it.

overridden.description: Whether this scope sets it itself, as opposed to inheriting.

default.description:
What the server scope held before anybody changed it: the value the
environment or the code gave it when the server began, which a change
is measured against and a reversal returns to. Said of the server
scope only, and never of a secret; absent for a setting that starts
unset, whose reversal is to set nothing.

EnteredPerson.description: Somebody as they are entered, or put right, by hand.

sortName.description:
What the index files and sorts them under, where it is not their
name: `Toro, Guillermo del`.

originalName.description: Their name in their own script: 宮崎駿.

image.description: Their portrait: an address a client can fetch.

aliases.description:
The other names they go by, typed by hand: those any other way —
their credits', TMDB's, a merged record's — are kept as they are.

EntryKind.description: What an entry of the chart is.

EpisodeCredit.description:
A credit on one episode of a series rather than on the series: a guest,
the director or a writer of that episode.

seasonNumber.description: Where the source numbers the episode.

tmdbEpisodeId.description:
TMDB's id of the episode: how the credit finds the episode it is of
in the work's own numbering, which may be TheTVDB's.

EpisodeHit.description: An episode found by its title.

workTitle.description: The series' title, in the language asked for where one is held.

EpisodeOrder.description:
One of the orders a series' episodes come in: one of TheTVDB's besides
the aired one, a TMDB episode group, one made here — or the aired order
itself, whose places are the work's own episodes and are not listed.

key.description:
What a client asks for it by — Sonarr v5's season type, Plex's
episode order, the TheTVDB relay's season type: `official` for the
aired order, TheTVDB's own type for its others (`dvd`, `absolute`,
`alternate`, `regional`, `altdvd`, `alttwo`), `tmdb-` and the id of a
TMDB episode group, `ams-` and a name for one made here.

source.description:
Where it was read: `tvdb`, `tmdb`, or `local` for one made here. The
aired order's is whoever numbers the work's episodes — `tmdb` while
TMDB numbers a series TheTVDB stopped answering for.

sourceRef.description: The order's id at its source: a TMDB episode group's.

label.description:
Its name: the series' own for one of TheTVDB's ("Superfan Order",
"BluRay Order") or TheTVDB's for the type ("DVD Order"), the group's
on TMDB, the one it was given here.

isDefault.description: Whether it is the aired order.

isFrozen.description:
Whether it is what the aired order answers with: Sonarr asking for
`official`, Sonarr v4, Plex with no order named and the TheTVDB relay
are given its numbering, frozen until it is thawed. One order of a
work at the most.

announced.description:
How many episodes its source says it holds, where they are yet to be
read: a TMDB group's are read the first time it is served or shown.

updatedAt.description:
When it was last written: read from its source, saved, frozen. An
episode that airs after it is served in a frozen or a home-made order
under its aired numbers, where the order leaves them free.

episodes.description:
Its places, in its own sequence. None for the aired order: its
places are the work's episodes.

tvdbShowId.description: Always written; never read, so not needed from the upstream either.

title.description:
Always written, `TBA` for an episode nobody has named yet (see
`episode_title`). Skyhook leaves it out then, and that is read as no
name: the episode, and the series, are kept.

ExportStarted.description: An export under way: where it writes, and the job run that records it.

jobId.description:
The run under `export.nfo` in the jobs list. Its detail, once it is
done, reads `N works, N episodes, N failed`; the settings page reads
the counts out of it.

ExternalIds.description: The identifiers known for one work, in the shape the compatibility surfaces need.

fankai.description: Fankai's id, for a Fan-Kai production; see `providers::fankai`.

wikidata.description: Wikidata's item, `Q1079`: a way to the work, never one to fetch it by.

Facet.description: One value a list can be narrowed to, and how many works it would leave.

slug.description:
A genre's slug, the same in every language: what its own page is
addressed by, `/genre/drama`. Only on the genres.

FacetKind.description: What a page of the catalogue is of.

FacetPage.description:
A page of the catalogue: a genre's, a network's or a studio's, a year's,
a decade's — what it is called, how many works it holds, the five rated
highest, how to list the rest, and what the programmer wrote about it.

slug.description:
What its address names it by: `drama`, `hbo`, `1999`, `1990`. A genre
asked for by another of its names, or a decade by another of its
years, is answered under this one, which the page's address becomes.

name.description:
What it is called: a genre in the reader's language where one is
known, a network as the works most often name it, a year and a decade
as their first year, which the interface words.

names.description:
A genre's names in every language known: `en`, `fr`, and `und` for
the one a source gave it by.

count.description: How many works it holds that the reader may see.

best.description: The five of them rated highest, as cards are drawn.

filter.description:
The list's own filters that list them all, for `/items` and
`/facets`: `{"genre": "drama"}`, `{"yearFrom": "1990", "yearTo": "1999"}`.

oneOf.description:
The programmer's note on it: in the reader's language, else in
English, else the one written last.

Facets.description: What the works on view can be narrowed by.

networks.description: Networks and studios together, most common first; the long tail left out.

languages.description: The languages works were made in, as stored.

FieldChange.description:
One value of a work that changed — of the work itself, of a season or of
an episode — as its journal writes it.

scope.description:
Where the value is, as a lock names it: `item`, `season:2`,
`episode:2x5` — an episode by the numbers it has after the change.

field.description:
The field, as the field registry names it; for an episode, `number`
when it moved, and `episode` when it came or went — `season` for a
season.

after.description: What it holds now, or would; `null` for nothing.

provider.description: The source whose answer the new value is, where one is known.

name.description: The entity's serde name; also the key stored in `media_override.field`.

label.description: Shown as the input label in the web UI.

translated.description:
The fields a lock may hold in one language alone, wherever a scope
has them: its texts.

FieldType.description: What a field holds. Drives validation here and the input widget in the UI.

addedRecently.description: Works added in the last thirty days.

decades.description: Works by decade of release, earliest first.

genres.description: The commonest genres, most common first.

networks.description: The commonest networks and studios, most common first.

languages.description: The languages works were made in, commonest first.

scores.description:
Works by the whole part of their score, lowest first: `7` is seven
point something.

keys.description: Keys the server let go of, all spaces together.

fankaiId.description: Fankai's id, for a Fan-Kai production.

stored.description:
Whether this server already holds it, so the interface can say "stored"
rather than offering to import it twice.

FurtherSources.description: What the further sources are working from.

oneOf.description: The anime identifier list; absent until it has been downloaded once.
IMDb's ratings; absent until they have been downloaded once.

The titles IMDb gives each work by region; absent until they have
been read once.

The episodes IMDb lists of each series; absent until they have been
read once.

Gaps.description:
How many works the register lists under each of its gaps: what each of
its filters would narrow it to, beside the filter.

poster.description: `missing=poster`: no poster of their own, nor one chosen by hand.

overview.description: `missing=overview`: no overview in the language they are stored in.

refresh.description: `missing=refresh`: never refreshed, though they could be.

divergingLock.description: `missing=divergingLock`: a lock a source moved under since it was set.

duplicates.description: `missing=duplicates`: in a pair proposed as one work.

mediaFailed.description: `missing=mediaFailed`: a picture or a theme the media store gave up on.

Group.description: What a row is about, for grouping.

instance.description: The instance that answered, by name.

leader.description: Which instance does, by name; none while no lease is held.

instances.description: How many instances were heard of lately, this one included.

sources.description: The sources, and whether each is switched on and able to answer.

jobs.description: The latest runs of the jobs, newest first.

oneOf.description: A newer release, when the check is on and found one; `null` else.

lastBackupAt.description:
When the newest archive of the database was made; `null` when none
was.

Hidden.description:
What the sources gave a work and a person hid. Served to nobody: kept
on the work as it is read, for whoever maintains the catalogue to show
again, and left out of every answer by

genres.description: Works carrying every one of these genres.

network.description: A network or a studio, by name.

minRating.description: A score out of ten the works must reach.

descending.description:

written out, so a form reads it back as the same thing.

How a list is composed: by hand, in an order, or by a filter evaluated as
it is read.

ListPlacement.description: How the works go into a selection.

Listed.description: An account in a list, with what it holds.

value it was set to.

fields.

unmatched.description: The works named that are not held here, by title.

Whether the account may maintain the catalogue, which decides where the

like an image's. Fankai keeps one for every Fan-Kai.

What TheTVDB adds to the series' name to tell it from another of the

The line the work is sold on, under its title — *Why are they here?* —

Every country the work was made in, ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 in upper case
— `US`, `GB` — in the order TMDB lists them.

is the first of them, or the one an anime source names instead.

What the provider that supplied this called it. Serving a catalogue
means being able to decide per request who sees it.

prequels, side stories — with the work here that each is, when the
catalogue holds it.

there: a country's, whole, from the first source that has any.

single episodes among it — and, read back, whom each credit is filed
under: see [`person::People`].

the sources gave is named as [`fields::Child`] names it.

the locks when the work is read; none by default.

when the work is read.

What the sources gave and a person hid: kept apart for whoever
maintains the catalogue, served to nobody.

background, the landscape and the logo a card or a plate shows —
before they are there: their size, the colour and the sketch they
are drawn as while they load, the AVIF copies made of them. By the
address the work gives each, and only for the copies this server
keeps. Set as the work is read for this server's own pages; never
stored, and never sent to a client elsewhere.

WebhookEvents.description: Every name a destination can be told of, besides `*`.

facts.description:
What happens on its own: a refresh failed, a medium given up on, a
newer release out.

actions.description: The actions of the audit trail, in the order its filter offers them.

defaults.description: What a new destination is told of, until other events are ticked.

kinds.description: The kinds of destination, in the order they are offered.

WebhookMessage.description:
One thing told, as a delivery keeps it: the event, who did it, to what,
what is worth saying of it, and when.

count.description:
How many things it tells of together — failed refreshes grouped for
a destination — when there are more than one.

WebhookRefusal.description: Why a test was not sent.

WebhookTest.description: What a test of a destination came to.

delivered.description: Whether the address took it: it answered, with a success.

status.description: What it answered with, when it answered.

error.description:
Why it was not reached, or what it said when it refused — in words
that name no address.

oneOf.description:
Why nothing was sent: `not_web`, not an http(s) address or one that
names this machine; `internal`, a name that resolves to an address
only reachable from here; `cleartext`, a token over plain http beyond
the home network; `unsent`, the post could not be made — a
standard destination without its secret — as `error` says.

millis.description: How long it took, in milliseconds.

link.description:
TMDB's page for the work in that country, which carries JustWatch's
own links to each service.

free.description: Free to watch, and free with advertising.

regions.description: Every country TMDB lists anything for, so a reader may ask for another.

attribution.description: Who the data comes from; shown beside it, as TMDB's terms ask.

WorkAlias.description: One name a merged work went by, as a reader of the survivor is told it.

source.description:
`id`, `slug`, or the source of an identifier elsewhere: `tvdb_series`,
`tmdb_movie`, `imdb`…

mediaId.description: The work that answers for it now.

mergedId.description: The work it named, kept as a tombstone.

title.description: Its title, in the language asked for where a translation is held.

matched.description:
The other name it was found by, where that is not its title: its
original title, one of its alternative ones.

WorkMedia.description: A work's media, and whether anything is kept at all.

store.description:
Whether a store is configured: without one, nothing can be uploaded
and nothing is fetched.

totals.description:
What they come to: how many are kept, waiting, given up on, and what
those kept weigh with their copies.

WorkMediaLine.description: A work, and what its media come to.

WorkMediaTotals.description: What one work's media come to.

pending.description: Waiting to be fetched, or tried again.

bytes.description: What the media kept weigh, in bytes.

copiesBytes.description:
What the copies made of its pictures weigh: the sizes the pages are
given, the night's AVIF.

WorkMedium.description: One address a work points at, and what is kept of it.

url.description: Where it is read from now: the copy kept, or the provider.

status.description:
`stored`, `pending`, `failed` — or `absent`, when nothing has been
asked of it: the store is off, or the address is not one it fetches.

WorkRef.description: A work named in passing — by an audit entry, a job — as a reader knows it.

bearer.description: The same key, as a bearer token.

session.name: ams_session
session.description: Set by /api/v1/auth/login. What the web UI uses.
